title: z-index cannot beat a host overlay in a sibling subtree — lift the mount to the shared ancestor, then order layers with the z token band
trigger: An injected overlay is visually/interactively under a host site's overlay even though its z-index looks high — and the host overlay element is not inside the same subtree as the injected one
principle: z-index only competes within a stacking context. If the host site keeps its own video overlays in a sibling subtree of the element you mount into (m.youtube: #player-control-container is a sibling of #player), no internal z-index — not even max-int — can paint your overlay above it; the parent context is compared as a whole. The root-cause fix is to mount into the shared ancestor that contains BOTH the video and the host overlay (appended last wins DOM-order ties), NOT to raise z-index. Then order extension surfaces with a semantic band: subtitle/video overlay at --z-overlay-video (10000) — above every host player layer (YouTube in-player max ~1000) — with transient in-container siblings at +1 (drag hint, OCR hitboxes), interactive selectors high (99998), portals/sheets at max-int, and body-level surfaces (dictionary popup, universal panel, dialogs) automatically above because they live outside the video container's stacking context. Always verify the same-size guard when lifting so inset:0 keeps tracking the video box, and beware lifted mounts escaping the playerShell that Player Mode / split view moves — that is why the lift is a guarded per-host adapter, not a generic farthest-ancestor walk.

cases.context: m.youtube: subtitle host (#Tihoka-subtitle-root, z:200) mounted inside #player; #player-control-container (native controls + scrim) is a sibling that paints above the entire #player subtree — subtitle under scrim, buttons unreachable.
cases.good:
findVideoOverlayContainer(video) → #player-container-id (shared ancestor,
same-size guarded) → host appended last + z-index: var(--z-overlay-video)
→ paints above host controls; body-level Tihoka surfaces still above it.

cases.context: Choosing the lift target — generic 'farthest same-size positioned ancestor' seems elegant but on desktop YouTube overshoots #movie_player to #player, which is OUTSIDE the playerShell that Player Mode/Split View physically moves — overlay gets orphaned in the vacated container.
Raising the subtitle host to --z-overlay-video (10000) silently re-orders in-container siblings that hardcoded z against the old 200 (e.g. .subtitle-drag-hint z:300 'above subtitle shadow host').
cases.bad:
host z → 10000; hint stays 300 → hint now painted UNDER the subtitle
band — 'drag to import' overlay invisible
cases.good:
bump siblings that must read above the host to calc(var(--z-overlay-video)+1)
(OCR overlay 10001 literal — foreign-document CSS can't use var()); check
every element in the same parent for stale 'above/below' assumptions.
